page: Microsoft Azure L64s_v4 is a storage-optimized instance running under Microsoft Hyper-V, designed for high-throughput I/O and data-intensive computing. The hardware configuration features an Intel Xeon 8573C processor built on the x86_64 architecture, providing 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores clocked at up to 4.2 GHz. The compute architecture integrates 260 MB of L3 cache alongside hardware support for Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 vector sets. It includes 512.0 GB of system memory, maintaining an 8.0 GB per-core allocation ratio, and is provisioned without dedicated GPUs.

Storage capability is anchored by 15,359 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD capacity, enabling direct, low-latency disk access for data storage workloads. Benchmark testing reflects high multi-threaded performance, with Geekbench multi-core scores placing in the top 10% (21,563.0) and PassMark CPU metrics reaching 73,408.39. Memory bandwidth tests demonstrate 225.0 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 96.91 GB/sec for writes. The instance delivers 93.83 GB/sec in static web serving and sustains 78.56 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations.

From an architectural standpoint, the instance balances high core density and substantial local NVMe storage against an absence of discrete GPU acceleration. Single-core performance falls largely within median tiers, whereas parallelized operations, database tests, and static throughput scale into the top quartile. Microsoft Azure L64s_v4 is technically tailored for distributed NoSQL databases, transactional data warehouses, large-scale Redis caching clusters, high-volume web serving, and CPU-driven batch processing requiring extensive low-latency local disk.
